name: Varlock
tagline: Validate environment variables and manage application secrets.
hook: Build ordering and paid review costs both become concrete rules for how agents work.
summary: Varlock's instructions cover the mechanics around a Bun and Turbo monorepo: dependency-aware builds, native binaries, tests, version bumps, and documentation. Several rules explain the cost they prevent. Filtered builds can miss workspace output; repeated pushes trigger paid reviews; rewriting technical examples during a tone edit can damage working documentation.

techniques.title: Explain the build dependency
techniques.body: The guide requires Turbo because downstream declaration bundling needs upstream build output. The prohibition is tied to a failure mode rather than a preferred spelling of the command.
techniques.quote: Do **not** build a package with `bun run --filter <pkg> build`: bun's filter does not build the package's workspace dependencies, and some builds require their dist output to exist (e.g. varlock's d.ts bundling inlines the emitted declarations from `packages/utils`, so it fails if that package was never built)

techniques.title: Read the local source of documentation
techniques.body: The public documentation service is for external users. Repository work is directed to the local docs, keeping edits and the material being consulted together.
techniques.quote: docs MCP server for external varlock users; do **not** use it to look things up while working on this repo — read the docs source directly

techniques.title: Treat pushes as a workflow cost
techniques.body: The contribution guidance connects each push to paid automated review. It asks for local iteration followed by a batch push, making the reason for the cadence visible.
techniques.quote: Pushes to open PRs trigger automated reviews that cost money.

techniques.title: Keep tone edits out of executable examples
techniques.body: Documentation guidance protects code fences and structured content while changing prose. That boundary lets an agent simplify language without silently changing commands.
techniques.quote: Never edit code fences, `ansi`/`diff` blocks, generated fixtures, frontmatter structure, or MDX component markup for tone. Prose only.

steal: Explain the dependency that makes one build entry point mandatory.
Point internal work at local documentation sources.
Document costly automation triggers where agents see commit and push guidance.
Define which parts of a document a prose-only edit may touch.
